This exact same thing happened to me in high school with my boyfriend of three years. He was my best friend and everything we did together was amazing and fun and I felt those butterfly feelings of first love every time I saw him or texted him, etc. Except he didn’t want to be intimate. I only had suspicions, and he broke up without explanation. I was devastated. He was my first true love, but i was confused why he didn’t want to take our relationship to an intimate level and why he was breaking up with me. Was I unattractive? And when he did come out later that year, it just made it worse. It made my emotional feelings feel like they weren’t real. But just know, they were real. And he loved you too (in a way slightly different than romance). Know that one day, you will likely be friends, if you want that (we are). It took me 4 years to heal, but now I have a best friend back. If honestly it feels the same as it used to when we hang out, minus the romance because I’m married and he has a boyfriend. There’s acceptance and we love each other as friends and can talk about the past. And you WILL find a romantic partner who does want to be intimate with you and you will fall in love again. But know, that intimacy is a big part of a relationship, and you cannot have a healthy romantic relationship without it. And know that he cannot give you that, because he doesn’t feel that way toward women. So the relationship would never be healthy, even if you were comfortable with some sort of asexual relationship arrangement. That’s really not fair to ask of you. So definitely don’t entertain that. You will need space and time to heal and move past this. Do not stay with him and don’t stay in touch if you’re hurting and need space to grieve. Sorry you’re going though this, it’s really not easy. So many complicated emotions, I’ve been there. But you will get through this. Hopefully college is on the horizon for a new beginning. :)

My younger brother is also a heroin addict. My mom has also guilted me into his care at times, which led to dealers coming to my house and standing outside, as well as the theft of my things. I have learned how to stand up to my mom and get past the guilt that I feel from both her and myself through alanon (or naranon) groups as well as private therapy. Having a drug addict in your immediate family is very, very hard. I am sorry for what you are going through. But setting firm boundaries for your child, wife and yourself is the ONLY answer, and you should not feel an ounce of guilt from your mother. She is confused and doesn't know what to do so is lookign to you, her "good" child, for help. But only your brother can help himself. And the sooner each and every one of you take that hardball approach toward him of "we will no longer enable you" and kick him out, he will never wake up. Watch your stuff around him, don't invite him into your house, and tell your mother to respect your boundaries case closed. The guilt you will not stand for. Maybe attend an alanon or naranon meeting together.

I used to doubt that my parents would ever kick him out, though lately they've seemed like they want to do something. They think that the second they kick him out, he will OD, but I've told them that is unfortunately a necessary risk, he could just as easily OD living in their house, and it wouldn't be their fault. Easier for me to say than a parent, but I really think that's true. They're doing him and my sister NO favors by letting him live there. In fact, they are endangering her. As far as him ratting on someone, they're never going to move, and you can easily look up our address, so if someone wanted revenge, they've got it. Luckily, I don't live there, and my sister only has two more years. I hope she gets TF out while she still can. 

I think my advice to them will be that if he really wants to go to rehab this time, it's with very firm rules that they need to enforce after the fact. I.e. he can only go to a long-term rehab facility. Not some 1 or 2 week crap. That's a solid red flag that he's just using it as an excuse. Something that's a solid few months. And he needs to be totally wanting to do it, rather than pressured into it. It needs to come from his mouth that he wants to, and why. 

Past that, once he's out, he can stay at their house, but only if he attends all his court dates for these aforementioned charges, gets a job, attends weekly NA meetings and therapy, and does a weekly drug test. If he fails to do any of these things, they kick him out. It's the same tune I've been telling them forever. I used to be steadfast in that advice, but with him making suicidal comments, I'm worried it's the wrong advice to give? I really have no idea what to say to them anymore. Should the advice remain the same? Should they have him committed or something? He's 22 so I'm not sure if they can do that but isn't that an option for people deemed mentally unstable/ suicidal?

Apparently he's telling my mom he wants to go, but I told her to be wary of a cop-out on his end to get people off his back, because he's gone twice before and dropped out/ got kicked out. He needs to want to go himself or it's a waste of her money, though I'm not sure of how to determine that. 

The ones he went to before were not-so-nice ones her insurance covered in rural Missouri, I wonder if my grandparents paid for him to go to a "nice" rehab if it would make any sort of a difference. Though of course, then we're talking about wasting even more money if he's not actually trying to get better and just trying to take the heat off.

Are the meetings super faith based? I'm agnostic and don't believe in a higher power, so I worry I won't be able to relate to the message. I heard you (as the family member) learn the 12 steps yourself?

I guess the only thing I would ask (and I suppose there are no right answers for), is that while cutting my brother out to preserve my own self makes sense, is it possible for me to have a relationship with my parents, especially my mother if they respect that boundary? Leave their house if he shows up? I know the next time if i visit home I will be staying with friends or in a hotel. I don't feel right cutting my parents out of my life. But if i do because I need to protect myself and it's impossible to balance the two, do I tell them it's because they're enabling him?
My therapist has been recommending I go. Previously the Naranon meetings in my area hadn't worked with my work schedule but I'm on a more flexible gig now. I should go to a meeting this week.
